## Design

### 2026-10-09 – ![Screenshot From 2026-10-10 07-34-07](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/Qgzhw9aCgZjWjX8UQ5PRuQQlkE5Sf2EF/3efbfc1b40019a1857255c085b7259bd5ee27abe2e32bf23fe088dcb869fecb

**2.03h**

![Screenshot From 2026-10-10 07-34-07](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Qgzhw9aCgZjWjX8UQ5PRuQQlkE5Sf2EF/3efbfc1b40019a1857255c085b7259bd5ee27abe2e32bf23fe088dcb869fecb3.png)

Today I started the Half-Life Week 1 project, designing the PCB for Starbie, a small desk pet with a XIAO ESP32-C3, an OLED screen, an MPU6050 motion sensor, a DHT11 temperature sensor and two buttons. I’m a complete beginner at electronics, so I followed the Week 1 Guide step by step.

Setup

Installed KiCad on my Linux machine.
Downloaded the Week 1 Care Package and extracted it into my project folder at Downloads/starbie. It contains a symbol library (Seeed_Studio_XIAO_Series.kicad_sym), a footprint folder (Imported Parts.pretty, with the OLED display, MPU6050 and XIAO footprints) and 3D models.
Created a KiCad project and added both libraries as project-specific libraries, so the parts show up in the schematic editor.

Schematic so far

Placed the XIAO-ESP32-C3-SMD as my microcontroller.
Added power symbols (+5V, +3.3V, GND) and wired them to the chip: VBUS to +5V and 3V3_OUT to +3.3V.
Found that the XIAO has three GND pins (13, 18 and 22), not one, and wired all three to ground. I also moved a GND symbol that had landed on top of the chip body.
Started the net labels for the signal pins: D1 for the DHT11 data, D2 and D3 for the buttons, D4 and D5 for the I2C lines (SDA and SCL).

Problem I found
The guide’s schematic picture puts SCL on D4 and SDA on D5, but its firmware table says the opposite (D4 is SDA, D5 is SCL). I also noticed that the guide on GitHub had been updated while I was working, so I’m going to check the current pin table before I finalize those two labels. Either order works electrically, as long as the schematic and the firmware pin numbers match.

### 2026-10-09 – I started the Half-Life Week 1 project: designing the PCB for Starbie, a desk pet with a XIAO ESP32-C3, an OLED, an MPU6050 motion sensor, a DHT11 sensor and two buttons. I’m a beginner at electronics

**2.02h**

I started the Half-Life Week 1 project: designing the PCB for Starbie, a desk pet with a XIAO ESP32-C3, an OLED, an MPU6050 motion sensor, a DHT11 sensor and two buttons. I’m a beginner at electronics, so I followed the Week 1 Guide step by step.

What I did

Installed KiCad on Linux.
Downloaded the care package into Downloads/starbie and imported its symbol library (Seeed_Studio_XIAO_Series.kicad_sym) and footprint library (Imported Parts.pretty).
Created the KiCad project and placed the XIAO-ESP32-C3-SMD in the schematic.
Added +5V, +3.3V and GND symbols and wired VBUS to +5V and 3V3_OUT to +3.3V.
Found that the XIAO has three GND pins (13, 18 and 22) and wired all of them.

Problems

The guide had been updated while I worked, so I re-read it.
The guide’s schematic picture puts SCL on D4 and SDA on D5, but its firmware text says the opposite. I decided to follow the picture and swap the pin numbers in the firmware later.

### 2026-10-10 – I finished the whole PCB design today and exported the manufacturing files.

**1.57h**

I finished the whole PCB design today and exported the manufacturing files.

Schematic

Added net labels from the guide’s picture: DHT11_DATA on D1, GPIO2 on D2, GPIO3 on D3, SCL on D4 and SDA on D5. Unused pins got no-connect flags.
Added both buttons (GPIO2, GPIO3 and GND), the OLED header, the MPU6050 header (pins 5 to 8 unused), the DHT11 and a 10k resistor on DHT11_DATA.
Assigned footprints from the guide’s picture, using the XIAO-ESP32-C3-SMD footprint from the care package.

PCB layout

Updated the PCB from the schematic and drew the board outline on Edge.Cuts.
Arranged the parts, then rearranged them so the traces were short and didn’t cross.
Routed all signal nets, then added GND pours on F.Cu and B.Cu.

Problems I solved

My first GPIO2 trace started on a GND pad and wouldn’t connect. The nets only appeared on the switch pads after I ran Update PCB from Schematic.
DRC showed one missing GND connection (U1 pad 13), and I connected it.

Result

DRC shows 0 unconnected items. The only 2 errors are the Footprint J1 courtyard errors that come from the care package footprint.
Exported Gerbers and drill files to the Gerbers folder (12 files).

Next: upload to GitHub, then do the firmware (swap the SDA/SCL pin numbers to match D4 = SCL and D5 = SDA).

### 2026-10-11 – I finished the firmware step. The board isn’t built yet, so I can’t upload it, but the code is ready and compiles.

**0.55h**

I finished the firmware step. The board isn’t built yet, so I can’t upload it, but the code is ready and compiles.

What I did

Read Starbie.ino from the guide’s repo and checked its pin constants against my schematic. The button pins (D2, D3) and the DHT11 pin (D1) already matched.
My schematic has D4 = SCL and D5 = SDA, but the sketch had them the other way round. I changed two lines so the firmware matches my PCB: I2C_SDA_PIN = 7 and I2C_SCL_PIN = 6.
Installed Arduino IDE, the ESP32 board package (esp32 by Espressif Systems) and the four libraries: Adafruit GFX, Adafruit SSD1306, Adafruit MPU6050 and DHT sensor library.
Selected the XIAO_ESP32C3 board and compiled the sketch.

Problems I solved

Arduino IDE wouldn’t open on Linux. The error was a chrome-sandbox permission problem, and starting it with --no-sandbox fixed it.
I closed the IDE by mistake, but my edits were saved in the file, so I reopened it with no loss.

Result

The sketch compiles with no errors. It uses 26% of program storage and 4% of memory.
I haven’t uploaded it, because I need the real board for that.
